answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake rising as its reputation grows. Like a jade seal pressed into wax, the stake proves the agent has real value at risk. An attacker flooding the ocean of the network with fake identities must fund each copy, and the cost climbs toward its zenith as verification fees peak at busy hours. Honest agents earn their stake back with interest, while detected fakes forfeit theirs, so mass fakery becomes unprofitable.
